subject: Discovery recap + pilot asks: Alveo integration & SDK changes
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@alveo.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 14:10:00 -0000
Subject: Discovery recap + pilot asks: Alveo integration & SDK changes

Hi Ethan —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap so we have alignment and clear next steps from both sides. High-level points we heard from your team: 

- Pain: Your support agents are overloaded with high-volume, repetitive triage requests; current reranking is noisy and latency-sensitive when returning suggested actions.
- Goal: Pilot to reduce deflection-to-resolution time by 30% and improve first-response usefulness for top-2 suggestions.
- Scope for pilot: 2-week live trial on a subset of incoming tickets (~10k/day), embeddings + reranking for retrieval, streaming responses for agent suggestions, and function-calling for structured action generation (create ticket, assign priority).

What Redwood will deliver for the pilot:
- A dedicated pilot environment (dedicated capacity) with an initial throughput target of 150 req/s and p95 generation latency target <=300ms for short contexts.
- SDK delta: small change to client SDK to support structured function outputs (we've attached redwood_sdk_delta_notes.md). We expect a minor client bump (patch-level) and a short integration task (~1 engineer for 2-3 days).
- Operational: network allowlist template, SOC2 artifacts, and sample SSO integration guide.

Open questions / asks from your side:
1) Can procurement review the MPA and SOW? (Procurement contact if different from CC'd).
2) Any data residency constraints we need to enforce for pilot data?
3) Please share a sample of your ticket payload (anonymized) so Rishi can validate schema for function-calling outputs.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Technical sync (60m) to walk through SDK changes, mock payloads, and deployment plan — suggested slots: Tue 9/29 10:00 or Wed 9/30 14:00 PT.
- We will send the pilot scope workbook (attached) and a network allowlist template for your infra team.
- Procurement: we'll send a draft SOW + MPA for review; Ben will be the point for commercial terms.

Attachments: Alveo_pilot_scope.xlsx, redwood_sdk_delta_notes.md, network_allowlist_template.txt

Thanks — look forward to next steps.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199

Appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side after internal sync: 

- Confirmed: primary KPI for pilot is reduction in agent handling time for triage flows; we'll share baseline metrics before kickoff.
- Data residency: must remain in us-west region for pilot; no export outside US.
- Procurement: please send the draft SOW and MPA to procurement@alveo.ai; they'll need standard indemnity language and a liability cap.

Technical asks:
- Could Rishi confirm expected token usage per ticket and an approximate cost estimate for the 2-week pilot? We need to validate budget with Finance.
- We're happy to provide an anonymized sample payload (ticket JSON) but want to be sure about sample retention — will Redwood retain the payloads after the pilot?

Tech sync: Tue 9/29 10:00 PT works for our engineering manager (Rachel) and me.

Thanks,

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@alveo.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + pilot asks: Alveo integration & SDK changes — technical notes

Ethan / Vanessa / team —

Following up with technical notes ahead of Tue's sync so we can be efficient: 

1) SDK changes (delta summary)- Add explicit function-calling contract support: 
  - New client API: callWithFunctions(payload, functionsSchema) => returns structured JSON with confidence scores.
  - Output format: topLevel { action: string, args: { ... }, confidence: float }
  - Backwards compatible: existing text-only paths remain unchanged.

2) Streaming vs non-streaming- We'll enable server-streaming for agent suggestions to improve perceived latency. If client cannot handle streaming, we recommend a 2-stage fallback: first return cached top-k embeddings results, then full rerank as a non-streaming call.

3) Batching & KV cache recommendations- Use micro-batches of ~16 concurrent requests for the pilot traffic profile; enable prefix KV caching for repeated user contexts to reduce tokens. This should keep p95 under target while saving unit cost.

4) Model selection & quantization- For the reranker and function-calling path we recommend a float16 Llama-3-13B variant (quantized profile q4_0) for the dedicated pilot nodes. We'll provide performance profile and token-cost estimate in the tech sync.

5) Data retention & logs- Pilot data will be ephemeral by default and accessible via the pilot console. Retention policy: 30 days unless you request deletion. We will include an opt-out retention flag for any sample payloads you share.

6) Cost estimate (ballpark)
- For 10k tickets/day over 14 days with the profile above, estimated raw inference token usage ~1.2B tokens. With dedicated capacity and the batching profile, expected pilot cost range: $6k–$11k depending on model variant. We will refine after seeing sample payload sizes.

Please upload an anonymized sample payload to the Drive folder before Tue so I can validate function schemas and token counts.

Looking forward to the sync —
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
